Refreshed review of the complete query_value claim, sole ordinary Stashed::new implementation association and complete lib.rs context, and sole associated TODO function sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_stash_storage_query_value. Compared the fresh whole-file implementation with the previously reviewed historical snapshot: the only delta replaces the scalar allocation debug assertion with an unconditional count!=1 collision skip and a safety explanation before read_one. This ensures scalar comparison uses a one-value entry, without changing root comparison, Salsa Update, or tracked boundaries. Rechecked current claim and association metadata and the complete associated test body; prior rationale remains applicable.

All requirements are accounted for: a stash-owned tree is one incremental value; root comparison/backdating occurs as a unit; internal nodes are not independent tracked identities; finer boundaries belong to semantic queries outside the tree. Stashed stores stash/root/fingerprint together, new fingerprints root-reachable content, PartialEq compares that fingerprint, and feature-gated Salsa Update retains the entire old root on equality or replaces the whole value on change. Ptr/Slice are internal indices, not tracked entities; their Update implementations do not introduce tracked identities or semantic query boundaries. The storage API supports the required unit boundary but does not itself demonstrate Salsa execution or downstream backdating.

The only associated test remains explicitly TODO and has no assertions. Its prerequisite is complete associated and reviewed integration query traces: producer reexecution with an equal reconstructed root must stop downstream invalidation, while changed reachable semantic content must change the root and invalidate consumers. Meaningful consumer execution assertions at external semantic-query boundaries remain necessary. An erroneous consumer rerun after equal reconstruction would evade the present placeholder; acceptance recognizes its explicit deferral, not implemented/tested end-to-end behavior. There are no N/A entries or other associated tests. The allocation fix does not discharge this TODO or introduce an additional claim-specific gap. No edits requested.

Source assessment and execution are separate: personally ran start, policy capture via review read, source/delta inspection, and record; no behavioral tests or build. Coordinator reports 331 sage-meta functional tests, 46 sage-stash tests, and workspace build passed, plus clean independent quality/sanity reviews. These are reported baseline results, not personal execution or proof of deferred query behavior. All implementation helpers used are inside the captured whole lib.rs; no uncaptured source helpers were relied upon.
